correctness.rationale: An independent pivoted maximal-clique search on the complement generates all inclusion-maximal independent sets. Every independent set is contained in one, so taking the union of their submasks gives exactly all possible all-positive query supports, with 11776 candidates. Exact distinct intersection counts against all 390 concepts reproduce 54/324/12 concepts at sizes 5/7/9 and shattered counts 1,27,270,1278,2862,2322 and zero at larger sizes. Removing all immediate subfaces of shattered supports leaves precisely 36 coordinate-transversal triples and 2322 quintuples; applying all 1296 coordinate/symbol permutations gives the stated orbit sizes. This is the full group: the three pairs of neighbors of 000 can be permuted and swapped within pairs, and an automorphism fixing 000 and those neighbors is forced on each successive distance layer by common neighbors of its predecessors. The exact maximum shattered size is five.
residual_risks: Only the 27-vertex ternary case; not a classification for larger orders or for maximum-only independent sets.

evidence: For triples (row,column,symbol), independence means no two triples agree in two coordinates: this is exactly a partial Latin square, and maximal independence means that no entry can be inserted. The complete-square class studied by Hatami–Qian has only 12 concepts at order three, versus 390 here.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A size spectrum for maximal partial squares does not determine whether a support realizes every trace. Complete squares cover only the maximum-size concepts, not the additional 378 incomplete maximal concepts.

originality.rationale: The distinctive content is the complete trace/facet classification of the class of inclusion-maximal order-three partial Latin squares. Prior work addresses possible concept sizes, complete Latin squares, binary cubes, neighborhoods or ordinary independence complexes. Those results are pertinent but do not establish the incidence patterns and orbits for the full 390-concept class.
residual_risks: Horák–Rosa chapter full text, the same-graph indexed topology result's full text, and the cited completion-paper DOI 10.1016/j.disc.2006.05.028 were not available in lawful OA attempts. In particular, older order-three array enumerations may overlap the concept census. The bounded comparison is not exhaustive priority certification.

value.rationale: The ternary order-three case is a natural small instance of maximal partial Latin squares, unlike a general collection of arbitrarily selected concepts. Finding triple facets that cannot extend even though many quintuples are shattered—and describing the triples by a complete coordinate-transversal rule—explains a concrete failure of purity. The exact polynomial and orbit refinement give a useful finite benchmark for that geometric phenomenon, independent of count-only results.
residual_risks: No broad assertion of nonpurity or maximum facet size across dimensions or alphabet sizes.
